created_roles.name: Fuel & Trucking Data Researcher
created_roles.description: A transport-economics researcher who pulls primary-source numbers from EIA and ATRI and records the exact series, dates and URLs. Careful about provenance and never fills gaps with invented values.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior transport-economics researcher. You have at most 5 turns per step, so plan the calls. TASK A (EIA): confirm via web_search, then fetch_url, the EIA weekly retail on-highway diesel price for the Midwest (PADD 2), series EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG, e.g. https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=emd_epd2d_pte_r20_dpg&f=w or the EIA Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update page. The history page is laid out by year and month with Week 1–5 columns, so map each cell to its Monday date. If the window spans two years, also fetch the previous year's page. Take the 52 most recent observations. Check that dates are consecutive Mondays (7 days apart) and that the latest is the most recent EIA release. Note that EIA publishes no Indiana state series; the Midwest PADD 2 series is the Indiana proxy. Write eia_midwest_diesel_52wk.csv (week_date, price_usd_per_gal, series_id, source_url, retrieved_date) with python/file tools. If you have no file tool, give the same 52 rows as an inline markdown table. If any week cannot be retrieved, mark it NOT FOUND and state the labelled substitute; never estimate silently. TASK B (ATRI): search 'ATRI An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' and identify the latest edition (year, release date, data year). Record total marginal cost per mile, fuel cost per mile and fuel share of total, with URL and retrieval date. If the fuel figure is not on any page you can fetch, say NOT FOUND and give the nearest sourced figure, labelled. Report in the specified formats; every figure needs a source and a date.
created_roles.goal: Deliver the 52 most recent EIA Midwest weekly diesel prices and the latest ATRI marginal cost figures, each with source, date and URL.
responsibilities: Locate the EIA weekly retail on-highway diesel series for the Midwest (PADD 2) and confirm series ID and units.
Extract the 52 most recent weekly values with dates and save them to CSV (or an inline table if no file tool).
Find the latest ATRI Operational Costs of Trucking edition: total marginal cost per mile, fuel cost per mile, fuel share, data year, publication date.
Record every gap or substitution explicitly.

outputs.format: csv columns: week_date (YYYY-MM-DD), price_usd_per_gal, series_id, source_url, retrieved_date
list: edition, data year, publication date, total marginal $/mile, fuel $/mile, fuel share, URL, retrieved date, gaps/substitutions

success_criteria: Exactly 52 consecutive weekly rows ending at the latest available Monday.
Series ID, URL and retrieval date are given for every row.
ATRI numbers come from the report or a reputable page quoting it, with edition year.
Any figure not found is labelled NOT FOUND with the substitute used.
constraints: No invented numbers.
Use only what the run's fetch_url and web_search return.
If fewer than 52 weeks can be retrieved, state the shortfall and what was used instead (e.g. EIA U.S. weekly series for the missing weeks, labelled).
If no file tool is available, output the 52 rows as an inline markdown table instead of a CSV.

created_roles.name: Fleet Cost Analyst
created_roles.description: A fleet finance analyst who builds formula-driven Excel models and clean charts, and reconciles every spreadsheet formula to an independent Python calculation.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior fleet finance analyst. You have at most 5 turns per step. WORKBOOK STEP: read the EIA CSV and the ATRI note. With openpyxl build: Inputs sheet (labelled cells tractors=35, miles_per_tractor_week=2300, mpg=6.2, base=1.25); Weekly sheet with columns week_date, price, series_id, surcharge_per_mile =ROUND((price-Inputs!base)/Inputs!mpg,2), fleet_miles, gallons, fleet_fuel_cost =gallons*price, fuel_cost_per_mile =price/mpg, optional surcharge_revenue; Bands sheet: lower bound 3.00 to 4.95 step 0.05, label like $3.00–$3.049, surcharge =ROUND((lower-base)/mpg,2), plus a '$5.00 and above' row at 5.00 (41 rows); Summary sheet: AVERAGE, MAX, MIN of price with INDEX/MATCH dates, total 52-week fuel cost, average fuel cost per mile (total cost ÷ total miles), ATRI total and fuel per mile and fuel share (values with edition, URL, date), differences in $ and %; Sources sheet: every source, series ID, URL, retrieval date, the Midwest-as-Indiana-proxy note, gaps and substitutions. Verify the files exist and the xlsx has formulas. KEY-FIGURES STEP: compute everything independently in Python with Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP from the CSV (never Python's round), write key_figures.json (average/high/low week with dates and surcharge, totals, 41 bands, carrier fuel $/mile, ATRI comparison, sources) and compare it with the workbook's formula logic (recalculate with LibreOffice if available, otherwise re-evaluate the formulas in Python). CHART STEP: matplotlib line chart, price on the left axis ($/gal) and surcharge on the right axis ($/mile) against week date; title naming the EIA Midwest PADD 2 series; legend; footnote 'EIA, retrieved <date>'; dpi 150, at least 1200 px wide. Check the PNG size with Bash. No invented numbers; carry any NOT FOUND labels through.
created_roles.goal: Produce the formula-driven workbook, key_figures.json and the PNG chart.
responsibilities: Build the xlsx with Inputs, Weekly, Bands, Summary and Sources sheets, using live formulas.
Compute the same numbers in Python (Decimal half-up), write key_figures.json and reconcile it with the workbook.
Draw the PNG line chart of price and surcharge.
inputs: eia_midwest_diesel_52wk.csv and the ATRI note (steps 1 and 2)

outputs.format: xlsx with formulas
json: average/high/low week with dates, band table, totals, carrier fuel $/mile, ATRI comparison, sources
png, at least 1200 px wide

success_criteria: Weekly sheet has 52 data rows with date, price, series ID, ROUND surcharge formula, gallons and fleet cost formulas.
Inputs (35, 2300, 6.2, 1.25) are live cells referenced by the formulas.
Bands sheet has 41 rows (40 bands + '$5.00 and above') with formulas.
Python values match the formula logic.
The chart has labelled axes, a legend, a title, dates and units.
constraints: Surcharge per mile rounded to the cent with ROUND(…,2).
No hard-coded results where a formula is possible.
Chart uses a secondary axis for price ($/gal) versus surcharge ($/mile).

created_roles.name: Memo Author
created_roles.description: A delivery lead who writes tight, decision-ready client memos in Word, fits dense tables into a hard page limit and cites every number.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior delivery lead writing a client memo in python-docx; you have at most 5 turns per step. DRAFT STEP: read key_figures.json. Structure: header (To/From/Date/Subject); first body paragraph exactly: 'I read "weekly retail on-highway diesel price for Indiana" as EIA's Midwest (PADD 2) weekly retail on-highway diesel price, used as the Indiana proxy because EIA does not publish a state-level Indiana series; if you meant An Indiana-specific weekly series, if one exists (e.g., a Midwest sub-series or a state-level listing) or EIA U.S. national average weekly retail on-highway diesel price as the fallback, the answer below may not apply. I read "5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00" as Bands $3.00–3.049, $3.05–3.099 and so on up to $5.00, with the surcharge at each band's lower bound; if you meant Discrete price points every $0.05 from $3.00 to $5.00 inclusive (41 rows) or Bands with the surcharge computed at the band midpoint, the answer below may not apply.' Then: (1) recommendation in 2–3 sentences and the formula (price − $1.25) ÷ 6.2, rounded to the cent; (2) 52-week statistics: average, highest and lowest weekly price with week dates and the surcharge at each, total and average fleet fuel cost; (3) ATRI comparison: ATRI total marginal and fuel $/mile and fuel share (edition, data year) against the carrier's average fuel $/mile, with a caution about different periods and bases; (4) sources and dates: EIA series ID EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG, URL, retrieval date and week range, ATRI report and URL; (5) gaps and assumptions: Midwest proxy, no discounts, all miles billed, NOT FOUND items and substitutes. Leave a placeholder for the band table. LAYOUT STEP: insert the band table in 3 side-by-side blocks (14, 14 and 13 rows plus a header), 41 rows in all, each with surcharge in $/mile at the lower bound. Margins 0.7 in. Convert to PDF (docx_to_pdf_page_counter or soffice --headless) and count pages; if the counter is unavailable, estimate by line count and state in your note that the page count is unverified. Trim until at most 2 pages.
created_roles.goal: Deliver a Word memo of at most 2 pages with the band schedule, statistics, ATRI comparison and full source and date trail.
responsibilities: Write the memo from key_figures.json and the cited notes only, without re-deriving numbers.
Lay out the 41-row band schedule compactly in side-by-side blocks.
Cite source and date for every figure.
State gaps, substitutions and assumptions, including both interpretation readings.
Check page length and trim to fit.
inputs: key_figures.json, chart PNG and workbook (steps 4 and 5)

outputs.format: docx, max 2 pages, with a table

success_criteria: The memo opens with the mandated interpretation text.
The band table covers $3.00 to $5.00 (41 rows).
It gives the average, highest and lowest week with dates.
It has an ATRI comparison with edition and year.
Every figure has a source and date.
A gaps/assumptions statement is present.
It is 2 pages or fewer (page count verified, or flagged as unverified).
constraints: At most 2 pages.
Body text 10 pt or larger, band table 9 pt or larger.
Use only figures from key_figures.json or the cited notes.

created_roles.name: Numbers & Sources Auditor
created_roles.description: An independent reviewer who recomputes results from raw inputs and checks that deliverables match the task. Does not trust the builders' outputs.
created_roles.prompt: You are a principal auditor; you have at most 5 turns. Independently verify. (1) Read the CSV: 52 rows, consecutive weekly dates, series ID EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG, plausible prices ($2.50–$6.00); spot-check 2–3 prices against EIA with fetch_url. (2) Recompute in Python with Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP: surcharge=(p-1.25)/6.2 rounded to the cent, weekly fleet cost = 35*2300/6.2*p, mean/max/min price and dates, total cost, average fuel $/mile, and the 41 band surcharges. Compare with key_figures.json and the workbook (openpyxl: formulas exist, input cells referenced, 52 data rows, 41 band rows). (3) Check the PNG exists, is at least 1200 px wide, and has both series. (4) Open the docx with python-docx: first paragraph begins with the mandated 'I read ...' text covering both readings and their alternatives, band table covers $3.00–$5.00, average/high/low weeks, ATRI comparison, source+date lines and gaps statement are present; count pages via docx_to_pdf_page_counter or soffice; if unavailable flag the page count UNVERIFIED. (5) Confirm ATRI numbers against the cited source. Output a table of checks, then 'VERDICT: PASS' or 'VERDICT: FAIL' with defects and which step to rerun.
created_roles.goal: Give a pass/fail verdict on data, calculations, files and memo, with a defect list.
responsibilities: Recompute surcharge, fleet cost, statistics and bands independently from the CSV.
Check that the workbook has formulas and matches the recomputed values.
Check the chart and memo against the requirements, page limit and citations.
Confirm the ATRI figures against the cited source.
inputs: All files and notes from steps 1–7

outputs.format: table: check x expected x found x pass/fail, then a VERDICT line (PASS or FAIL) with defects and the step to rerun

success_criteria: Independent recompute matches key_figures.json to the cent.
52 rows with consecutive dates.
The memo has at most 2 pages (or the count is flagged unverified) and includes the mandated opening line.
Every figure is cited and dated.
A verdict is stated.
constraints: Must not edit the producers' files; report defects only.
Reproduce the recomputation with code, not by eye.
If the page counter is unavailable, flag the page count as UNVERIFIED rather than pass it.

## Requirements:
R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for the most recent 52 weeks from EIA (Midwest PADD 2 as the Indiana proxy). Cite the series ID and the week date of every price.
R2: For each of the 52 weeks, compute the fuel surcharge per mile = ROUND((price − 1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2) and the fleet's total fuel cost for that week.
R3: Find the latest ATRI 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' average marginal cost per mile and the share of it that is fuel (fuel $/mile component). Compare them with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.
R4: Deliver an Excel workbook with the weekly price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost, using live formulas.
R5: Deliver a PNG line chart of price and surcharge over the 52 weeks.
R6: Deliver a Word memo of at most 2 pages that gives the average, highest and lowest week, the ATRI comparison, and the source and date of every figure.
R7: State any figure that could not be obtained and what was used instead. Never invent data.
R8: Open the final answer with the mandated interpretation line (both readings, with the alternatives under which the answer may not apply).
R9: The carrier runs 35 Class 8 tractors (heavy-duty semi tractors over 33,000 lb GVWR) that average 6.2 mpg and about 2,300 miles per week each. Base the fuel-surcharge schedule and the fuel-cost picture on this fleet, with 35, 2,300, 6.2 and the $1.25 base as live input cells.
R10: Give the surcharge for each 5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00 (bands $3.00–3.049, $3.05–3.099 … up to $5.00), computed at each band's lower bound, in the workbook (with formulas) and in the memo.
R11: Read 'weekly retail on-highway diesel price for Indiana' as EIA's Midwest (PADD 2) weekly retail on-highway diesel price, used as the Indiana proxy because EIA does not publish a state-level Indiana series. Disclose this in the workbook Sources sheet, the memo and the final answer.

- Weekly fleet fuel cost = gallons × weekly price = 12,983.87 × price (equivalently miles × price ÷ 6.2).
- Carrier fuel cost per mile in a week = price ÷ 6.2. The 52-week average = total 52-week cost ÷ 4,186,000 = mean price ÷ 6.2.

## Requirements:
R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for the most recent 52 weeks from EIA (Midwest PADD 2 as the Indiana proxy). Cite the series ID and the week date of every price.
R2: For each of the 52 weeks, compute the fuel surcharge per mile = ROUND((price − 1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2) and the fleet's total fuel cost for that week.
R3: Find the latest ATRI 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' total marginal cost per mile and its fuel component (and fuel share). Compare them with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.
R4: Deliver an Excel workbook with the weekly price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost, using live formulas.
R5: Deliver a PNG line chart of price and surcharge over the 52 weeks.
R6: Deliver a Word memo of at most 2 pages containing: the surcharge for each 5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00; the average, highest and lowest week; the ATRI comparison; and the source and date of every figure.
R7: State any figure that could not be obtained and what was used instead. Never invent data.
R8: Open the final answer with the mandated two-sentence interpretation line (Midwest/PADD 2 proxy; bands at lower bound).

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Fleet = 35 Class 8 tractors; 6.2 mpg; 2,300 miles per tractor per week.
- Fleet miles per week = 35 × 2,300 = 80,500. Fleet gallons per week = 80,500 ÷ 6.2 ≈ 12,983.9. Annual (52 wk) miles = 4,186,000; gallons ≈ 675,161.
- Weekly fleet fuel cost = gallons × weekly price = 12,983.87 × price. Equivalent: miles × price ÷ 6.2.
- Fleet fuel cost per mile in a week = price ÷ 6.2. The 52-week average = total 52-week cost ÷ 4,186,000 miles = mean price ÷ 6.2.
- Surcharge = ROUND((P − 1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2). At the band edges: $3.00 → 1.75/6.2 = 0.2823 → $0.28; $5.00 → 3.75/6.2 = 0.6048 → $0.60. Each 5-cent step adds about 0.8 cent.
- Bands from $3.00 to $5.00 in 5-cent steps = 40 bands ($3.00–3.049 … $4.95–4.999), plus an '$5.00 and above' row = 41 rows. The memo table must be compact (e.g. two or three side-by-side column blocks) to stay within 2 pages.
- Weekly surcharge revenue (optional) = surcharge × 80,500 miles, assuming every mile is billed (assumption).
- EIA Midwest (PADD 2) weekly retail on-highway diesel series ID: EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG (dollars per gallon, released Mondays/Tuesdays). To be confirmed by the researcher on eia.gov.
- ASSUMPTION: the Midwest PADD 2 price is the Indiana proxy (EIA publishes no Indiana state series).
- ASSUMPTION: fleet fuel cost uses the EIA retail price, with no fleet discounts, taxes or card rebates, and all miles are fuel-burning at 6.2 mpg.
- ASSUMPTION: the latest ATRI edition is whichever is newest at run time (likely the 2025 edition covering 2024 data). Its cost year differs from the carrier's 52-week window, and the memo must say so.

- question: Does the carrier want the Indiana price proxied by the Midwest PADD 2 average? | assumption: Yes; settled by the working interpretation. The memo discloses it.
- question: Should each band's surcharge be computed at the lower bound, the midpoint, or at discrete $0.05 points? | assumption: Lower bound of each band, as settled.
- question: What fuel price does the carrier actually pay (discounts, tax exemptions, fuel-card rebates)? Only the carrier can supply this. | assumption: The EIA retail price is the paid price.
- question: Are all 80,500 weekly miles billable, loaded and empty? | assumption: Yes for the surcharge schedule. Surcharge revenue is shown only as an illustration.

## Risks and Decisions:
- EIA pages may not be fetchable or parseable in 5 turns, and the EIA API needs a key. Fallback: parse the dnav history page, or use search snippets for the latest weeks, and clearly state any weeks that remain missing. Decision point at step 1: if fewer than 52 weeks of PADD 2 data are retrievable, label any U.S.-average substitute weeks and carry that into the memo (R7).
- The ATRI full report may be behind a form or hard to read, so the fuel $/mile figure may only be available through secondary coverage. Fallback: cite the secondary source and label it. Decision point at step 2.
- The Midwest PADD 2 average differs from the Indiana price (Indiana is often a little higher than the PADD 2 average), so surcharges may under- or over-recover. This is disclosed in the memo.
- The ATRI cost year differs from the carrier's 52-week window and ATRI's fuel price/mpg basis differs from the carrier's, so the comparison is indicative only. The memo says so.
- Excel ROUND half-up differs from Python round half-even, so cent values could mismatch. Use Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP in Python and have the verifier recheck.
- The 41-row band table plus a full memo could exceed 2 pages. Use side-by-side column blocks, narrow margins and a PDF page count. If it still exceeds 2 pages, re-run step 4 after trimming; the verifier flags this.
- If the step 5 verdict is FAIL, re-run the step named in the defect list (3 or 4), then re-verify before step 6.
- The carrier's actual fuel price, discounts and billable-mile share are unknown, so the fleet cost is a retail-price estimate.

## Requirements:
R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for the most recent 52 weeks from EIA (Midwest PADD 2 as the Indiana proxy). Cite the series ID and the week date of every price.
R2: For each of the 52 weeks, compute the fuel surcharge per mile = ROUND((price − 1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2) and the fleet's total fuel cost for that week.
R3: Find the latest ATRI 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' average marginal cost per mile and the share of it that is fuel (fuel $/mile component). Compare them with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.
R4: Deliver an Excel workbook with the weekly price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost, using live formulas.
R5: Deliver a PNG line chart of price and surcharge over the 52 weeks.
R6: Deliver a Word memo of at most 2 pages that gives the average, highest and lowest week, the ATRI comparison, and the source and date of every figure.
R7: State any figure that could not be obtained and what was used instead. Never invent data.
R8: Open the final answer with the mandated interpretation line. It covers both readings: the Midwest/PADD 2 proxy for the Indiana price, and the 5-cent bands at the lower bound. It also names the alternative readings (Indiana-specific series or U.S. national fallback; discrete $0.05 points or band-midpoint surcharge) under which the answer may not apply.
R9: Base the fuel-surcharge schedule and the fuel-cost picture on the carrier's fleet: 35 Class 8 tractors (heavy-duty semi tractors over 33,000 lb GVWR) averaging 6.2 mpg and about 2,300 miles per week each, as live input cells.
R10: Give in the memo the surcharge for each 5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00 (bands $3.00–3.049, $3.05–3.099 … up to $5.00), computed at each band's lower bound rather than at the midpoint, in the workbook (with formulas) and in the memo.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Fleet = 35 Class 8 tractors; Class 8 = heavy-duty trucks over 33,000 lb GVWR (semi tractors); 6.2 mpg; 2,300 miles per tractor per week.
- Fleet miles per week = 35 × 2,300 = 80,500. Fleet gallons per week = 80,500 ÷ 6.2 ≈ 12,983.87. Over 52 weeks: miles = 80,500 × 52 = 4,186,000; gallons ≈ 675,161.
- Weekly fleet fuel cost = gallons × weekly price = 12,983.87 × price (equivalently miles × price ÷ 6.2).
- Carrier fuel cost per mile in a week = price ÷ 6.2. The 52-week average = total 52-week cost ÷ 4,186,000 = mean price ÷ 6.2.
- Surcharge = ROUND((P − 1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2). At the band edges: $3.00 → 1.75/6.2 = 0.2823 → $0.28; $5.00 → 3.75/6.2 = 0.6048 → $0.60. Each $0.05 step adds 0.05/6.2 ≈ 0.8 cent.
- Band step = $0.05. Bands run $3.00–3.049, $3.05–3.099, … , $4.95–4.999. That is (5.00 − 3.00) ÷ 0.05 = 40 bands, plus an '$5.00 and above' row = 41 rows, with lower bounds 3.00, 3.05, … 4.95, 5.00. The memo table must be compact (2–3 side-by-side blocks) to fit 2 pages.
- Optional illustration: weekly surcharge revenue = surcharge × 80,500 miles, assuming every mile is billed (assumption).
- EIA Midwest (PADD 2) weekly retail on-highway diesel series ID: EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG ($/gal, Monday price dates). The researcher confirms it on eia.gov.
- ASSUMPTION: Midwest PADD 2 is the Indiana proxy (EIA publishes no Indiana state series), as the working interpretation settles.
- ASSUMPTION: fleet fuel cost uses the EIA retail price with no discounts, tax exemptions or card rebates, and all miles burn fuel at 6.2 mpg.
- ASSUMPTION: the latest ATRI edition is whichever is newest at run time. Its cost year differs from the carrier's 52-week window, and the memo says so. ATRI's fuel price and mpg basis differ from the carrier's, so the comparison is indicative.

- Rounding: Excel ROUND is half-up, so Python checks use Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP.

## Requirements:
R1: Get the weekly retail on-highway diesel price for the most recent 52 weeks from EIA (Midwest PADD 2 as the Indiana proxy). Cite the series ID and the week date of every price.
R2: For each of the 52 weeks, compute the fuel surcharge per mile = ROUND((price − 1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2) and the fleet's total fuel cost for that week.
R3: Find the latest ATRI 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' average marginal cost per mile and the share of it that is fuel (fuel $/mile component). Compare them with the carrier's average fuel cost per mile over the 52 weeks.
R4: Deliver an Excel workbook with the weekly price, surcharge and fleet fuel cost, using live formulas.
R5: Deliver a PNG line chart of price and surcharge over the 52 weeks.
R6: Deliver a Word memo of at most 2 pages that gives the average, highest and lowest week, the ATRI comparison, and the source and date of every figure.
R7: State any figure that could not be obtained and what was used instead. Never invent data.
R8: Open the final answer with the mandated interpretation line (both readings, with the alternatives under which the answer may not apply).
R9: The carrier runs 35 Class 8 tractors (heavy-duty semi tractors over 33,000 lb GVWR) that average 6.2 mpg and about 2,300 miles per week each. Base the fuel-surcharge schedule and the fuel-cost picture on this fleet, with 35, 2,300, 6.2 and the $1.25 base as live input cells.
R10: Give the surcharge for each 5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00 (bands $3.00–3.049, $3.05–3.099 … up to $5.00), computed at each band's lower bound, in the workbook (with formulas) and in the memo.
R11: Read 'weekly retail on-highway diesel price for Indiana' as EIA's Midwest (PADD 2) weekly retail on-highway diesel price, used as the Indiana proxy because EIA does not publish a state-level Indiana series. Disclose this in the workbook Sources sheet, the memo and the final answer.
R12: Read '5-cent price band from $3.00 to $5.00' as bands $3.00–3.049, $3.05–3.099 and so on up to $5.00, with the surcharge at each band's lower bound. Disclose this in the memo and the final answer.
R13: In the opening line, name the alternative readings under which the answer may not apply: an Indiana-specific weekly series, if one exists (e.g., a Midwest sub-series or a state-level listing), or the EIA U.S. national average as the fallback; discrete $0.05 price points (41 rows) or a band-midpoint surcharge.
R14: Plan the delivery before building it: record assumptions, open questions and risks; have an independent reviewer check numbers, sources and files; and report the verdict and any unresolved defects in the final answer.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Fleet = 35 Class 8 tractors; Class 8 = heavy-duty trucks over 33,000 lb GVWR (semi tractors); 6.2 mpg; 2,300 miles per tractor per week.
- Fleet miles per week = 35 × 2,300 = 80,500. Fleet gallons per week = 80,500 ÷ 6.2 ≈ 12,983.87. Over 52 weeks: miles = 80,500 × 52 = 4,186,000; gallons ≈ 675,161.
- Weekly fleet fuel cost = gallons × weekly price = 12,983.87 × price (equivalently miles × price ÷ 6.2).
- Carrier fuel cost per mile in a week = price ÷ 6.2. The 52-week average = total 52-week cost ÷ 4,186,000 = mean price ÷ 6.2.
- Surcharge = ROUND((P − 1.25) ÷ 6.2, 2). At the band edges: $3.00 → 1.75/6.2 = 0.2823 → $0.28; $5.00 → 3.75/6.2 = 0.6048 → $0.60. Each $0.05 step adds 0.05/6.2 ≈ 0.8 cent.
- Band step = $0.05. Bands run $3.00–3.049, $3.05–3.099, … , $4.95–4.999. That is (5.00 − 3.00) ÷ 0.05 = 40 bands, plus a '$5.00 and above' row = 41 rows, with lower bounds 3.00, 3.05, … 4.95, 5.00. The memo table must be compact (3 side-by-side blocks of 14, 14 and 13 rows) to fit 2 pages.
- Optional illustration: weekly surcharge revenue = surcharge × 80,500 miles, assuming every mile is billed (assumption).
- EIA Midwest (PADD 2) weekly retail on-highway diesel series ID: EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG ($/gal, Monday price dates). The researcher confirms it on eia.gov.
- ASSUMPTION: Midwest PADD 2 is the Indiana proxy (EIA publishes no Indiana state series), as the working interpretation settles.
- ASSUMPTION: fleet fuel cost uses the EIA retail price with no discounts, tax exemptions or card rebates, and all miles burn fuel at 6.2 mpg.
- ASSUMPTION: the latest ATRI edition is whichever is newest at run time. Its cost year differs from the carrier's 52-week window, and the memo says so. ATRI's fuel price and mpg basis differ from the carrier's, so the comparison is indicative.
- ASSUMPTION: the carrier's fuel share of its own total cost cannot be computed (no carrier total cost given). The memo compares carrier fuel $/mile with ATRI fuel $/mile and ATRI fuel share. It may also show carrier fuel $/mile as a % of ATRI total, labelled illustrative.
- Rounding: Excel ROUND is half-up, so Python checks use Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP.

- question: Should each band's surcharge be computed at the lower bound, the midpoint, or at discrete $0.05 points? | assumption: Lower bound of each band, as settled. The memo states the other readings may change the numbers.
- question: What fuel price does the carrier actually pay (discounts, tax exemptions, fuel-card rebates)? Only the carrier can supply this. | assumption: The EIA retail price is taken as the price paid; the memo flags this.
- question: Are all 80,500 weekly miles billable (loaded and empty)? | assumption: Yes for the schedule. Surcharge revenue is shown only as an illustration.

roles.prompt: You are a senior transport-economics researcher. You have at most 5 turns per step, so plan the calls. TASK A (EIA): confirm via web_search, then fetch_url, the EIA weekly retail on-highway diesel price for the Midwest (PADD 2), series EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG, e.g. https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=emd_epd2d_pte_r20_dpg&f=w or the EIA Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update page. The history page is laid out by year and month with Week 1–5 columns, so map each cell to its Monday date. If the window spans two years, also fetch the previous year's page. Take the 52 most recent observations. Check that dates are consecutive Mondays (7 days apart) and that the latest is the most recent EIA release. Note that EIA publishes no Indiana state series; the Midwest PADD 2 series is the Indiana proxy. Write eia_midwest_diesel_52wk.csv (week_date, price_usd_per_gal, series_id, source_url, retrieved_date) with python/file tools. If you have no file tool, give the same 52 rows as an inline markdown table. If any week cannot be retrieved, mark it NOT FOUND and state the labelled substitute; never estimate silently. TASK B (ATRI): search 'ATRI An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' and identify the latest edition (year, release date, data year). Record total marginal cost per mile, fuel cost per mile and fuel share of total, with URL and retrieval date. If the fuel figure is not on any page you can fetch, say NOT FOUND and give the nearest sourced figure, labelled. Report in the specified formats; every figure needs a source and a date.

roles.prompt: You are a senior fleet finance analyst. You have at most 5 turns per step. WORKBOOK STEP: read the EIA CSV and the ATRI note. With openpyxl build: Inputs sheet (labelled cells tractors=35, miles_per_tractor_week=2300, mpg=6.2, base=1.25); Weekly sheet with columns week_date, price, series_id, surcharge_per_mile =ROUND((price-Inputs!base)/Inputs!mpg,2), fleet_miles, gallons, fleet_fuel_cost =gallons*price, fuel_cost_per_mile =price/mpg, optional surcharge_revenue; Bands sheet: lower bound 3.00 to 4.95 step 0.05, label like $3.00–$3.049, surcharge =ROUND((lower-base)/mpg,2), plus a '$5.00 and above' row at 5.00 (41 rows); Summary sheet: AVERAGE, MAX, MIN of price with INDEX/MATCH dates, total 52-week fuel cost, average fuel cost per mile (total cost ÷ total miles), ATRI total and fuel per mile and fuel share (values with edition, URL, date), differences in $ and %; Sources sheet: every source, series ID, URL, retrieval date, the Midwest-as-Indiana-proxy note, gaps and substitutions. givens: Fleet = 35 Class 8 tractors; Class 8 = heavy-duty trucks over 33,000 lb GVWR (semi tractors); 6.2 mpg; 2,300 miles per tractor per week.
Fleet miles per week = 35 × 2,300 = 80,500. Fleet gallons per week = 80,500 ÷ 6.2 ≈ 12,983.87. Over 52 weeks: miles = 80,500 × 52 = 4,186,000; gallons ≈ 675,161.
Weekly fleet fuel cost = gallons × weekly price = 12,983.87 × price (equivalently miles × price ÷ 6.2).
Carrier fuel cost per mile in a week = price ÷ 6.2. The 52-week average = total 52-week cost ÷ 4,186,000 = mean price ÷ 6.2.

Band step = $0.05. Bands run $3.00–3.049, $3.05–3.099, … , $4.95–4.999. That is (5.00 − 3.00) ÷ 0.05 = 40 bands, plus a '$5.00 and above' row = 41 rows, with lower bounds 3.00, 3.05, … 4.95, 5.00. The memo table must be compact (3 side-by-side blocks of 14, 14 and 13 rows) to fit 2 pages.
Optional illustration: weekly surcharge revenue = surcharge × 80,500 miles, assuming every mile is billed (assumption).
EIA Midwest (PADD 2) weekly retail on-highway diesel series ID: EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG ($/gal, Monday price dates). The researcher confirms it on eia.gov.
ASSUMPTION: Midwest PADD 2 is the Indiana proxy (EIA publishes no Indiana state series), as the working interpretation settles.
ASSUMPTION: fleet fuel cost uses the EIA retail price with no discounts, tax exemptions or card rebates, and all miles burn fuel at 6.2 mpg.

ASSUMPTION: the latest ATRI edition is whichever is newest at run time. Its cost year differs from the carrier's 52-week window, and the memo says so. ATRI's fuel price and mpg basis differ from the carrier's, so the comparison is indicative.

ASSUMPTION: the carrier's fuel share of its own total cost cannot be computed (no carrier total cost given). The memo compares carrier fuel $/mile with ATRI fuel $/mile and ATRI fuel share. It may also show carrier fuel $/mile as a % of ATRI total, labelled illustrative.
Rounding: Excel ROUND is half-up, so Python checks use Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP.
risks: EIA pages may not be fetchable or parseable in 5 turns, and the EIA API needs a key. Fallback: parse the dnav history page, or use search snippets for the latest weeks. Decision point at step 1: if fewer than 52 PADD 2 weeks can be retrieved, label any U.S.-average substitute weeks and carry that into the memo (R7).

The ATRI full report may be behind a form, so the fuel $/mile figure may only be available through secondary coverage. Fallback: cite the secondary source and label it. Decision point at step 2.
The Midwest PADD 2 average differs from the Indiana price, so surcharges may under- or over-recover. This is disclosed in the memo.
The ATRI cost year and its fuel price/mpg basis differ from the carrier's 52-week window and 6.2 mpg, so the comparison is indicative only. The memo says so.
Excel ROUND half-up differs from Python round half-even. Use Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP and have the auditor recheck.

The 41-row band table plus the full memo could exceed 2 pages. Use side-by-side blocks, 0.7 in margins and a PDF page count; step 7 trims. If the page counter is unavailable, the count is flagged unverified and the auditor does not pass it.
